identity.title: Markov Chain Monte Carlo without Evaluating the Target: an Auxiliary Variable Approach

problem.claim: Develop MCMC methods for sampling when evaluating even the unnormalized target distribution is costly or infeasible.

contributions.claim: Unifies the exchange algorithm, PoissonMH, and TunaMH under a common procedure.
Introduces a framework using auxiliary variables in both proposal and acceptance–rejection steps, yielding gradient-guided MCMC algorithms.
Develops theory for the framework and uses it to simplify and extend results for existing algorithms.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe the auxiliary-variable framework as novel, including auxiliary variables in both proposal and acceptance–rejection steps.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report significantly better performance for the resulting algorithms than existing methods on synthetic and real datasets.
The authors report theoretical results that simplify and extend results for existing algorithms.

narrative_sequence.summary: Target distributions may be known only up to normalization, while evaluating the unnormalized distribution can itself be costly or infeasible.
The difficulty is described for Bayesian posteriors on tall datasets and doubly-intractable distributions.
Several seemingly different MCMC algorithms are first unified through a common procedure.
That procedure is extended into an auxiliary-variable framework, producing gradient-guided algorithms and associated theory.
The new algorithms are reported to outperform existing methods on synthetic and real datasets.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a computational bottleneck to a unifying procedure, then to a framework extension, algorithm instances, theory, and empirical comparisons.

lessons.interpretation: This sequence makes the relationship between motivation, construction, analysis, and evidence traceable.
lessons.application: Structure a method abstract by explicitly mapping the initial bottleneck to a shared abstraction, its extension, resulting instances, and separate theoretical and empirical outcomes.
lessons.exception: This structure is unsuitable when a paper has no genuine unifying abstraction or when theory and experiments do not directly concern the proposed method.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the performance metrics, dataset details, baselines, or conditions behind the reported significant improvement.
It does not state the precise theoretical guarantees or how auxiliary variables are sampled and used.
The claimed novelty and experimental results are author-reported and not independently verified here.
